title: Nonparametric Identification and Estimation of Causal Effects on Latent Outcomes
abstract: arXiv:2604.08681v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: How should researchers conduct causal inference when the outcome of interest is latent and measured imperfectly by multiple indicators? We develop a general nonparametric framework for identifying and estimating average treatment effects on latent outcomes in randomized experiments. We show that latent-outcome estimation faces a fundamental but overlooked noncomparability problem due to measurement-set dependence: adding, removing, or replacing measurement targets a different transformation of the latent outcome and therefore a different causal estimand. We formalize the (non)comparability problem and show that common procedures in practice, including standardized averages, principal components analysis, and inverse covariance weighting, generally do not satisfy this condition. To address the problem, we propose a design-based approach built around nonparametric bridge functions. We characterize when such bridge functions exist

translated_title: 潜在结果因果效应的非参数识别与估计
translated_abstract: 当所关注的结果是无法直接观测的潜在结果，且只能通过多个指标被不完美地测量时，研究者应如何进行因果推断？我们开发了一个通用的非参数框架，用于在随机实验中识别和估计潜在结果的平均处理效应。我们证明，由于测量集依赖性，潜在结果估计面临一个根本性但长期被忽视的不可比性问题：添加、删除或替换测量指标会使估计目标指向潜在结果的不同变换，从而对应不同的因果估计量。我们对（非）可比性问题进行了形式化，并表明实践中常用的方法，包括标准化均值、主成分分析和逆协方差加权，通常不满足这一可比性条件。为解决该问题，我们提出了一种围绕非参数桥函数构建的基于设计的方法，并刻画了此类桥函数存在的条件。
tldr: 该论文揭示了多指标测量潜在结果时因测量集变化导致的不可比性问题，并提出基于非参数桥函数的设计方法，实现了随机实验中潜在结果平均处理效应的非参数识别与估计。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a fundamental noncomparability problem in estimating causal effects on latent outcomes measured by multiple indicators, and proposes a design-based approach using nonparametric bridge functions to enable identification and estimation of average treatment effects in randomized experiments.
